page: Google Cloud Platform n4-standard-48 is a general-purpose virtual machine designed for balanced compute and memory workflows. It operates on x86_64 Intel processors equipped with 48 vCPUs across 24 physical cores, supporting hyper-threading with 2 threads per core. Memory allocation is configured at 192 GB of RAM, yielding a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio with 4.0 GB per core. The processor features 48 KB of L1d cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and a large 260 MB L3 cache. It incorporates advanced ISA capabilities, including AVX-512, AVX-VNNI, and Intel AMX (Advanced Matrix Extensions with amx_tile and amx_int8) alongside hardware encryption acceleration via AES, VAES, and SHA-NI.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong parallel throughput across multi-core computing tasks. While single-thread operations fall within average tiers—scoring 1,869 in Geekbench single-core and 1,783.48 in stress-ng—the server registers top-quartile performance in Geekbench multi-core (17,663.0) and PassMark CPU metrics (58,480.28 overall, 59,197.94 for extended instructions). Memory bandwidth for large blocks is also elevated, showing 259.28 GB/sec in read and 114.19 GB/sec in write tests. The presence of AMX accelerates INT8 matrix calculations, reflected in top-tier prompt processing speeds of 2,557.3 tokens per second for small models (135M) and 183.37 tokens per second for medium models (7B).

Hardware tradeoffs center on storage and graphics acceleration. The n4-standard-48 contains zero GPUs and provides no bundled local NVMe storage, requiring network-attached persistent disks for all non-volatile storage needs. Network attachment configuration also omits complimentary public IPv4 addresses. However, its high vCPU density, substantial uncached memory bandwidth, and high static web serving throughput (67.45 GB/sec) make it an efficient host for large-scale enterprise microservices, clang software build pipelines, PassMark-tested database workloads, and CPU-driven quantized model inference.
description: Google Cloud Platform n4-standard-48 is a general-purpose instance featuring 48 vCPUs and 192 GB of RAM across 24 physical Intel cores on the x86_64 architecture. Configured with a balanced 1:4 core-to-memory ratio and 260 MB of L3 cache, it supports AVX-512 and AMX instructions for accelerated matrix workloads. The machine includes no local storage or GPUs, relying entirely on network-attached storage. Benchmark evaluations show top-quartile performance in multi-core compute tasks, such as software compilation, ray tracing, and large-block memory read/write throughput reaching 259.28 GB/sec and 114.19 GB/sec respectively. High static web serving throughput and efficient PassMark database metrics underscore its capacity for compute-heavy parallel workloads. Google Cloud Platform n4-standard-48 is suited for large database services, continuous integration build clusters, and CPU-based machine learning inference.
